title: Cairo Geniza bifolio with Hebrew-letter and glyph cipher blocks, Cambridge University Library T-S AS 187.240

documents.shelfmark: Cambridge University Library, Taylor-Schechter Additional Series 187.240 (PGP 42435)

plaintext.source: No edition or reading found (Hebrew-script sweep, 6 Nov 2026).

transcription.notes: First pass of the Hebrew-letter block only, from a downsized crop, doubtful letters marked ?. The glyph block (about 120 signs) and the plain Hebrew lines are not transcribed. Counts cover the Hebrew-letter block only.

system.summary: Hebrew-letter word groups in dotted words and a block of invented glyphs, probably one formula in two codes; system not established.
system.notes: Strings of 2-4 Hebrew letters that are not Hebrew words, repeated on several lines; the second glyph unit repeats the first.

prior_solution.where: No reading found in the Princeton Geniza Project, DECODE, Tomokiyo, Lasry or the sweep's literature check; Cambridge's catalogue and the Geniza researchers (Elbaum, Bohak) not yet asked. PGP record 42435 read 6 Nov 2026: pen-trial bifolio, no transcription, translation or bibliography.

conditions.human_role: The user chose this target from the Arabic and Hebrew sweeps and asked for an attempt.

solution.what: Hebrew-script sweep: Princeton Geniza Project cipher tag, Bohak 2010, Cambridge Genizah blog, DECODE harvest, Tomokiyo, Schmeh; no reading of AS 187.240 found.
Fetched both Cambridge IIIF images by curl (2000 px); looked at crops of the glyph side.
First-pass transcription of the Hebrew-letter block (28 words, 15 distinct) from a downsized crop, with doubtful letters marked.
Fetched native-resolution IIIF tiles (5286 x 4628) of both sides; lines legible but cursive letters ambiguous.
Recurring two- and three-letter groups compared by eye with the 72 trigrams of the Shem ha-Meforash as a possible known plaintext; not tested on a checked transcription.
Second pass at native resolution: ten lines of side 1, doubtful letters marked; letters ambiguous on crops.
Eyeball comparison of recurring groups with the 72 trigrams and the 42-letter name; no run of three groups matched; not a computed test.

Tokens of the repeated formula (final forms collapsed) tested as substrings of the 42-letter name and the 72 trigrams against shuffled baselines: 42-letter name 5 of 15 hits, P=0.002; 72 trigrams no signal. Post hoc, doubtful readings.
Three subagents transcribed side 1 blocks A-D, side 2 Hebrew lines and the glyph block (28 glyph codes); low to medium confidence.

Isomorph search of the 19-letter Hebrew frame (and halves) against every window of the 72 trigrams and the 42-letter name: no match; glyph formula checked for alignment with the Hebrew frame: 7 words vs 9, no parallel.
All 21 alphabet shifts, atbash, albam, ayak-bekar and reversal applied to the 9-group frame; no running Hebrew.

outcome.method_basis: Not attempted beyond a first transcription: the usable ciphertext is small and the system is not yet identified.
outcome.notes: In progress. Needs a clean transcription at native resolution, a reading of the plain Hebrew lines as cribs, and contact with Elbaum and Bohak.
